# Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 6 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Bodmer V / Greek MSS, Proto-Gospel of James 6 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/POX_006_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 6

**6:1** The child grew strong day by day. When she was six months old her mother set her on the ground to test whether she could stand. She walked seven steps and came to her mother's bosom. And her mother caught her up, saying: "As the Lord my God lives, you shall walk no more on this ground until I bring you into the temple of the Lord."

**6:2** And Anna made a sanctuary of her bedchamber and suffered nothing common or unclean to pass through it. She called the undefiled daughters of the Hebrews, and they played with her.

**6:3** On the child's first birthday, Joachim made a great feast and invited the priests and scribes and elders and all the people of Israel. He brought the child to the priests, and they blessed her, saying: "O God of our fathers, bless this child and give her an everlasting name to be named in all generations." And all the people said, "So be it, amen."

**6:4** He brought her to the chief priests, and they blessed her, saying: "O God Most High, look upon this child and bless her with an ultimate blessing which cannot be surpassed."

**6:5** Her mother carried her up into the sanctuary of her bedchamber and gave her suck. And Anna made a song to the Lord God, saying: "I will sing a holy song to the Lord my God, for he has visited me and taken away the reproach of my enemies. The Lord God has given me the fruit of his righteousness, single and manifold before him. Who shall tell the sons of Reuben that Anna gives suck? Hear, hear, O twelve tribes of Israel: Anna gives suck."

**6:6** And she laid the child to rest in the sanctuary of her bedchamber and went out and ministered to the guests. When the feast was completed they went away rejoicing and glorifying the God of Israel.

---

## Translator's Note

Anna's song in 6:5 is a deliberate echo of Hannah's song in 1 Samuel 2, cementing the typological parallel between the two mothers. The "seven steps" in 6:1 are rich in symbolic resonance — seven being the number of completion. The ritual purity maintained around Mary's room begins the motif of her consecration that will culminate in the temple dedication.
